output.title: Decreasing Students’ Stress Through Time Management Training

scenes.narration: This paper asks whether a short time management training can reduce undergraduate students’ perceived stress and increase their perceived control of time.
scenes.layout_description: Center one student between a tangled clock and a calmer planner, with orange arrows moving from chaos to order.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn black ink line art on solid cream background: a student at a desk, one side surrounded by messy clock spirals, the other by a neat calendar, with orange and yellow highlights.

scenes.narration: The authors begin from concern that university students often report stress, citing previous studies on student mental health and stress levels worldwide.
scenes.layout_description: Place a worried student under a stack of papers, with small citation cards floating around them.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal black ink drawing of a student holding their head beneath papers and books, surrounded by small paper notes, with orange circles emphasizing stress marks.

scenes.narration: They note that earlier studies connected heightened perceived stress with underachievement, dropout, illness, depression, and unhealthy coping among students in various samples.
scenes.layout_description: Show stress as a central knot with thin arrows pointing to several simple warning icons.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink line art of a large tangled knot labeled stress, with arrows to icons of a falling grade sheet, exit door, sick bed, sad face, and bottle, orange accents only.

scenes.narration: The paper focuses on time-related demands, such as high workload, time pressure, and self-organized learning, as serious problems previously reported for many students.
scenes.layout_description: Arrange three simple icons around one student: books, a clock, and a lone study desk.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn student juggling books, a clock, and a notebook, with orange arrows showing pressure from all sides on a clean cream background.

scenes.narration: Time management interventions are recommended in student support programs, but the authors emphasize that evidence about training effectiveness is scarce, especially for students.
scenes.layout_description: Contrast a help desk offering a calendar with a small empty evidence shelf beside it.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink sketch of a university support desk handing a planner to a student, next to a nearly empty shelf labeled evidence, with yellow highlight on the gap.

scenes.narration: Their research question was whether time management training could increase perceived control of time and reduce perceived stress in a student sample.
scenes.layout_description: Put the research question visually as two arrows from a training box toward control and stress gauges.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal line drawing of a box marked training, with one orange arrow raising a control gauge and another arrow lowering a stress gauge.

scenes.narration: They hypothesized that perceived control of time would increase, perceived stress would decrease, and perceived, self-reported demands would remain unchanged after training.
scenes.layout_description: Use three side-by-side meters showing up, down, and flat movement.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn three simple meters: control needle rising, stress needle falling, demands needle flat, with orange arrows and yellow highlights.

scenes.narration: The study used a non-equivalent dependent variable design: one trained group, two intended outcome variables, and one control variable for comparison within participants.
scenes.layout_description: Show one group of students branching into three measured paths.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink drawing of one small student group, with three arrows leading to clipboards for stress, control, and demands; orange highlights mark the comparison.

scenes.narration: Perceived stress was measured with the tension scale, covering mental fatigue, trouble relaxing, and nervousness that should be affected by training here.
scenes.layout_description: Place a tension clipboard beside icons for tiredness, restless relaxation, and nerves.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal ink illustration of a clipboard labeled tension, with a drooping head, a tense chair, and jitter lines around hands, orange marks showing focus.

scenes.narration: Perceived control of time covered feeling in control, estimating task time, and avoiding procrastination, using an adapted ten-item scale from prior research.
scenes.layout_description: Show a student holding a clock, a task list, and a checked plan.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink line art of a student calmly holding a clock and checklist, with an orange check mark and a small avoided delay symbol.

scenes.narration: Demands was the control variable, measuring perceived work amount and external duties, because the training did not aim to change external demands.
scenes.layout_description: Draw outside demands as unchanged objects pressing toward the student from the margins.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn student at center, with books and duty papers pushing inward from outside, while a no-change flat orange line sits beneath them.

scenes.narration: The training lasted for 4 h and focused on prioritizing, goal setting, strategy development, daily planning, and monitoring as its major parts.
scenes.layout_description: Show a four-hour clock surrounding five small training activity icons.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal black ink clock labeled 4 h around icons for priority star, goal flag, path steps, daily calendar, and check marks, with yellow highlights.

scenes.narration: Students first reflected on academic and extracurricular activities, considered their importance for study goals, and identified the most important ones for themselves.
scenes.layout_description: Show students sorting activity cards into a highlighted important pile.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink drawing of hands moving cards for study, clubs, and tasks into piles, with the important pile circled in orange.

scenes.narration: Next, they defined concrete, challenging, proximal goals, set deadlines, developed steps, prioritized steps, planned starts, and considered obstacles and responses to them.
scenes.layout_description: Use a path from a goal flag through ordered steps and around a small obstacle.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn path with numbered stepping stones, a flag at the end, a small rock obstacle, and an orange detour arrow around it.

scenes.narration: Daily planning asked what to do, when and where to do it, how much time to schedule, and how to avoid distractions.
scenes.layout_description: Show one day calendar with time blocks and a distraction crossed out.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal ink drawing of an open daily planner with time blocks, a location pin, and a phone-like distraction crossed by an orange line.

scenes.narration: The final part instructed trainees to monitor tasks each day, seeing what they completed and what still had to be done next.
scenes.layout_description: Place a checklist with completed items and a small next-task arrow.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink line art of a checklist on a desk, several boxes ticked in orange, one empty box with a yellow arrow pointing forward.

scenes.narration: Forty-eight local undergraduates began, but the main analyses used the 23 students who completed questionnaires at all three measurement points in total.
scenes.layout_description: Show a larger group narrowing to a smaller group beside three clipboards.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn group of 48 represented by many simple heads fading to 23 highlighted heads, next to three clipboard icons, orange funnel arrow.

scenes.narration: The 23 students had a mean age of 23.30 years, SD=2.80, studied different subjects, and about half, 52 %, were female overall.
scenes.layout_description: Arrange simple student portraits around a university building with subject symbols.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal black ink portraits of students around a small university building, with tiny icons for varied subjects and an orange circle around half the portraits.

scenes.narration: Participants attended in the middle of the semester, in groups of about ten students, with one trainer experienced in time management training.
scenes.layout_description: Show a trainer at a board with a small group seated in a semicircle.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn classroom scene with one trainer pointing to a calendar board, about ten simple student figures seated, orange highlight on the group.

scenes.narration: The measures were taken directly before training, 2 weeks after training, and 4 weeks after training, within the same external context throughout.
scenes.layout_description: Use a simple timeline with three measurement stops and the same campus background behind all stops.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink timeline with three clipboard stops labeled before, 2 weeks, and 4 weeks, all under the same small campus outline, orange dots on stops.

scenes.narration: Before training, most students reported no or little experience using time management strategies; one reported some more experience, and none quite a lot.
scenes.layout_description: Show a row of experience jars, mostly low-filled, one slightly higher, none full.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal ink drawing of jars labeled experience, most with low yellow fill, one with a modest fill, and an empty full-level mark.

scenes.narration: After training, trainees reported significantly more use of taught strategies at 4 weeks, and a nearly significant increase at 2 weeks as well.
scenes.layout_description: Show strategy use rising across three points, with the final point highlighted strongest.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn small line chart with three dots rising from before to 2 weeks to 4 weeks, final dot circled orange and middle dot lightly highlighted yellow.

scenes.narration: For the intended outcomes, the MANOVA showed a significant overall time effect from pretest to 2 weeks after training in the study.
scenes.layout_description: Draw two outcome gauges moving together between pretest and two weeks.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink illustration of two gauges labeled stress and control connected to a before-to-2-weeks arrow, with an orange burst marking overall change.

scenes.narration: At 2 weeks, perceived stress measured with tension was significantly lower, while perceived control of time showed a tendency in the expected direction.
scenes.layout_description: Show a stress thermometer dropping and a control arrow nudging upward but not fully highlighted.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal line art of a tension thermometer with orange level lower, beside a control gauge with a faint upward yellow arrow.

scenes.narration: At 4 weeks, there was a significant overall time effect, with significantly less tension and significantly more perceived control of time reported.
scenes.layout_description: Show two clearly changed gauges at four weeks, one down and one up.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn paired gauges: tension needle clearly down and control needle clearly up, both circled in orange on a clean cream background.

scenes.narration: Perceived, self-reported demands did not change significantly from pretest to 2 weeks or from pretest to 4 weeks after training in analyses.
scenes.layout_description: Place the demands line flat across three measurement points beneath unchanged workload icons.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink drawing of books and duty papers staying the same size above a flat orange line connecting before, 2 weeks, and 4 weeks.

scenes.narration: The authors conclude training might benefit undergraduate well-being, but call the study preliminary because samples must be larger for robust conclusions later.
scenes.layout_description: End with a cautious takeaway: a student holding a planner beside a small seedling labeled future research.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal hand-drawn student calmly holding a planner, next to a small growing plant and a larger empty research plot, with warm orange and yellow highlights.
